## 🔴 Errors (Will Cause Build Failures or Incorrect Behavior)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — Line 10: `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `.props` is dead code (AP-21)

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (like LibA and LibB), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation — it's only set once the project file itself is read. This condition **never matches**, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is never set to `true`.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is evaluated *after* the project file:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Lines 7–10: Properties override project-level settings

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `.targets` is imported *after* the project file. Unconditional property assignments here **override** any project-level setting. LibB explicitly sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` (line 13), but this `.targets` file silently forces it back to `true`. The project-level opt-out has no effect.

**Fix:** Move default properties to `Directory.Build.props` with a conditional default pattern:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 3. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Line 13: Unquoted condition value

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The condition is missing quotes around both the property expansion and the value. If `$(Configuration)` is empty, this evaluates to ` == Debug` which is an MSBuild evaluation error. Even when set, string comparisons should be quoted.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 4. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Line 14: `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This replaces *all* existing constants (`DEBUG`, `TRACE` from the SDK). Code relying on `#if DEBUG` will silently break in Debug builds.

**Fix:**
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 5. `LibA/LibA.csproj` — Lines 43–45: Publish-on-build re-invokes same project (bin/obj clash)

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** This forks a second evaluation of the same project with an additional global property. Both instances write to the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`, causing a race condition (file-in-use errors) and double work. This is a well-known anti-pattern (AP-22).

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish within the *same* project instance, guarded by a property:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);PublishAfterBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="PublishAfterBuild" Condition="'$(DesignTimeBuild)' != 'true'">
  <!-- publish logic here -->
</Target>
```

---

### 6. `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj` — Lines 7–9: Wrong file compilation order

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

**Problem:** In F#, **file order is the compilation order**. `Services.fs` references `BrokenOrder.Domain` (`open BrokenOrder.Domain`), but `Domain.fs` is listed *after* it. This will produce a compile error: `FS0039: The namespace or module 'BrokenOrder.Domain' is not defined`.

**Fix:** Reorder so dependencies come first:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />

**Problem:** Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, any project that references LibA or LibB as a package will transitively inherit StyleCop.Analyzers — imposing your code-style rules on downstream consumers.
